category: feature flags, experimentation and product analytics (hosted)

free_tier.stated: Developer tier, free: 2 million metered events every calendar month at no charge, with free access to feature gates, dynamic configs, experimentation and core product analytics, and 1 year of analytics data retention; past 2 million events gate and config targeting keeps working and metric lift computation stops
free_tier.notes: The unit is the metered event: an SDK call that logs an event, an exposure check with metric lift enabled, an ingested metric or a custom metric. The vocabulary has no events term, so requests is the nearest. An account starts on the Developer tier at sign-up; the Pro tier is USD 150 a month with 5 million metered events.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no per-event or per-request size is stated on the pages read

retention.stated: 1 year of data retention for analysis on the free tier, against unlimited on Pro

egress.terms: unverified: the pricing page lists a data export API (export exposure, event and result data) but its captured text does not show which tier includes it

interface_detail: A Console API at statsigapi.net (CRUD for what the console does) takes a Console API key in the STATSIG-API-KEY header; an HTTP API takes a server-side secret key or a client SDK key in the statsig-api-key header, with every call a POST and a JSON body. SDKs are recommended over the HTTP API.
tooling: the SDKs, the HTTP API, the Console API and the web console
chaining: Feature gates, dynamic configs and experiments for a free-hosted app, with the first 2 million metered events a month free and product analytics in the same project.

limits.value: 2 million metered events per calendar month on the Developer tier
1 year of analytics data retention on the free tier
Console API: about 1,800 request attempts per 15-minute window per project for mutation requests, with burst protection

limits_note: Gates and configs keep evaluating past the monthly events, while metric lift computations stop after warning notifications.
binding_note: The 2 million metered events a month is the ceiling for an app with traffic, and exposure checks count against it as well as logged events.

identity_cost.detail: An account starts on the Developer tier at sign-up and a credit card is asked only when the 2 million events are exceeded. Which sign-in methods the sign-up form offers is unverified: its page text shows no form; any phone step is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: past the free events, metric lift computations stop after several warning notifications while gate and config targeting continues
confidence_note: The free allowance, the card prompt and the retention are quoted from the first-party pricing FAQ and the API limits from its documentation. No account was opened, so the sign-up fields are unverified: behind a sign-up.

evidence.proved: an account starts on the free Developer tier with 2 million metered events a month at no charge
evidence.quote: When you first sign up for Statsig, you automatically start on Statsig’s Developer Tier, which gives you free access to gates, configs, experimentation and analytics. On this plan, you get 2 million Metered Events (see definition below) every calendar month at no charge.

evidence.proved: a credit card is asked only when the 2 million event limit is exceeded
evidence.quote: If you exceed the 2 million Developer Tier events limit, you’ll be shown a prompt to enter a credit card to upgrade to Statsig’s Pro tier.

evidence.proved: on the Developer tier gate and config targeting continues while metric lift computations stop
evidence.quote: If you want to stay on the Developer tier, gate and config targeting will continue to work, but Metric Lift computations will stop.

evidence.proved: warning notifications precede the end of metric lift computations
evidence.quote: You will be sent multiple warning notifications before Metric Lifts are no longer calculated.

evidence.proved: the free tier includes core product analytics with 1 year of data retention
evidence.quote: On the free tier that includes our Core Product Analytics features and 1 year of data retention for analysis.

evidence.proved: an exposure check with metric lift and a logged event are metered events
evidence.quote: Log event: When an application calls the Statsig SDK to log an event or when an event is imported to Statsig from a 3rd party source (e.g. Segment)

evidence.proved: the Pro tier has a baseline fee of USD 150 a month
evidence.quote: On Statsig’s Pro tier, you will be charged a baseline fee of $150 per month at the start of each billing period.

evidence.proved: the Pro tier includes 5 million metered events a month
evidence.quote: Statsig’s Pro Tier includes 5 million Metered Events per month.

evidence.proved: the Console API is the CRUD API for what the console does without the web UI
evidence.quote: The Console API is the CRUD API for performing the actions available on console.statsig.com without using the web UI.

evidence.proved: SDKs are recommended over the HTTP API
evidence.quote: Statsig strongly recommends using an official SDK for your programming language whenever possible.

evidence.proved: the Console API is served at statsigapi.net
the Console API takes a key in the STATSIG-API-KEY header
evidence.quote: All requests must include a Console API key in the `STATSIG-API-KEY` header.

evidence.proved: the Console API allows about 1,800 mutation request attempts per 15 minutes per project
evidence.quote: The default quota is approximately 1,800 request attempts per 15-minute window.

evidence.proved: the HTTP API authenticates with a statsig-api-key header and takes POST requests with a JSON body
evidence.quote: Authenticate using the `statsig-api-key` header. All API requests use the POST method, and you pass parameters as a JSON object in the request body.

evidence.proved: the HTTP API documentation tells the reader to create a free account
evidence.quote: Create a free account on the [Statsig sign-up page](https://statsig.com).

notes: Past the free events the offered upgrade is the Pro tier at USD 150 a month, which includes 5 million metered events a month.
